Topic: Superposition and Quantum States: The Architecture of Reality

Target audience: Undergraduate science students or scientifically curious high schoolers

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide

Lecture lines:
Classical states are either here or there.
Quantum states represent possibilities as a vector.
We call this quantum state vector, |ψ>.
Think of a coin blurring between heads and tails.
Quantum reality exists as a multi-dimensional mathematical space.

Planned animations:
FadeIn classical bit as a single Dot (color #FF0000).
Label classical bit as '0' or '1' using Text.
Transform classical bit into a superposition Dot (color #00FF00).
Display coefficients alpha and beta next to Dot.
Highlight superposition Dot with a pulsating glow effect.

Section: section_2 — Defining Superposition: The Linear Combination

Lecture lines:
Superposition combines basis states linearly.
The state is a sum: |ψ> equals α|0> plus β|1>.
Visualize this arrow pointing anywhere on a sphere.
Like a chord blending notes C, E, and G.
The state lives on the Bloch sphere surface.

Planned animations:
Initialize state vector |psi> as a vertical vector.
Draw two basis states |0> and |1> in light gray (#D3D3D3).
Animate alpha and beta as scalar weights on basis vectors.
Sum these components to show vector |psi> orientation.
Flash final combined vector |psi> to emphasize linear combination.

Section: section_3 — Visualizing Probability Amplitudes

Lecture lines:
Amplitudes squared give us probability densities.
Waves interfere, reinforcing or canceling outcomes.
A robot explores every maze path simultaneously.

Planned animations:
Draw a unit circle centered at origin (color #FFFFFF).
Represent probability amplitudes as complex numbers on the plane.
Fade in phasor arrows (color #FFFF00) rotating for phase visualization.
Highlight the modulus squared as the area of a sector.
Sync sector area change with rotating phasor arrow.

Section: section_4 — Measurement and Wavefunction Collapse

Lecture lines:
Measurement forces the system to choose.
The Bloch vector snaps to one pole.
Schrödinger's cat collapses from both to one.

Planned animations:
Show superposition state vector pointing between axes.
Animate measurement operation as a vertical projection onto axes.
Collapse state vector onto either |0> or |1> instantly.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: Why it Matters

Lecture lines:
Superposition enables massive quantum parallelism.
Qubits calculate all possibilities at once.
A quantum computer sees the whole library instantly.

Planned animations:
Display the full Bloch sphere overview in center.
Flash key concepts previously discussed: superposition, measurement.
Fade out all elements leaving only the title card.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lines = [
            "Classical states are either here or there.",
            "Quantum states represent possibilities as a vector.",
            "We call this quantum state vector, |ψ>.",
            "Think of a coin blurring between heads and tails.",
            "Quantum reality exists as a multi-dimensional mathematical space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide", lines)
        
        # --- Mobjects ---
        classical_dot = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        
        superposition_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        coeff_text = MathTex(r"\alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle", font_size=30, color="#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        self.wait(1)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Why it Matters", [
            "Superposition enables massive quantum parallelism.",
            "Qubits calculate all possibilities at once.",
            "A quantum computer sees the whole library instantly."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        label_sp = Text("Superposition", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        label_meas = Text("Measurement", font_size=24, color=RED)
        
        bloch = VGroup(sphere, dot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(bloch, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(bloch), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(label_sp, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label_sp))
        self.play(Indicate(bloch))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_meas, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(label_meas))
        self.play(FadeOut(bloch), FadeOut(label_sp), FadeOut(label_meas))
        self.wait(1)
